cohort: 678 women undergoing periviable birth (23 0/7-25 6/7 weeks gestation)
finding: Attempting a vaginal delivery for periviable births (23 0/7-25 6/7 weeks) was associated with decreased risks of maternal infectious morbidity and shorter hospital stays compared to planned cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Attempting a vaginal delivery for periviable births was associated with decreased risks of endometritis, fever, maternal thrombosis, and shorter hospital stays compared to planned cesarean delivery.
